title: About the Project
text:
What this is
This project treats The Brothers Karamazov as a computational humanities corpus while preserving a distinction between textual observation and interpretation.

title: About the Project
text:
Epistemic model
Observed — directly derived from the text, such as a character mention or co-occurrence.
Machine-proposed — a computational interpretation that has not yet been human validated.
Human-validated — an assertion reviewed against its textual evidence.

text:

SPOILER-AWARE LITERARY RAG


Ask Dostoevsky
Ask about a character, conflict, idea, symbol, or moral question in The Brothers Karamazov.
The answer will use a simulated Dostoevskian literary voice, while its claims remain grounded in passages from the novel available at your current I’ve read through… position.

Literary simulation. Generated responses are not quotations from Dostoevsky. Direct quotations from the novel will be identified separately and linked to their source passages.








DOSTOEVSKY · SIMULATED VOICE


You have opened the book and disturbed its people from their arguments. Very well. Ask what troubles you. But remember: a man rarely asks a question without revealing something of himself in the asking.







Reading boundary loading…


Ask Dostoevsky






TRY ASKING



What does Ivan seem to believe about human freedom?


How does Alyosha respond to suffering?


What is driving the conflict between Dmitri and his father?


What has the novel said about faith and doubt so far?


What should I notice about the Karamazov family?




EVIDENCE RULE


The model may only receive passages at or before your selected reading boundary. Later passages are excluded before retrieval.
